OCTOBER FIELD LOG — CAT HEAD AREA, LAKE MARION

This is a retrospective of our firsthand October fishing trips, not a claim that the same fish are holding there today. October's fishing gave us a documented starting point for evaluating the seasonal move into November.

OCTOBER 5 — Our trip produced approximately 240 pounds of catfish, including four fish over 50 pounds. Wind was reported around 7 mph from the north-northeast to north-northwest. These are trip totals, not a lakewide catch forecast.

OCTOBER 13 — Fishing near Cat Head, morning surface water temperature was about 75.7°F. Bait was observed in approximately 10–18 feet of water. The recorded catch included a 6-pound channel catfish and an 8-pound blue catfish, followed by a blue reported around 40 pounds later in the trip.

OCTOBER 21 — Near Cat Head, water temperature ranged from approximately 70.3°F to 72.8°F during the trip. We caught blue catfish weighing approximately 30 and 25 pounds in about 18 feet of water, and later a blue around 40 pounds in approximately 22 feet on an upslope.

WHAT THE LOG TELLS US — During the documented October outings, productive water included bait-related structure and depth changes in the upper-teen to low-20-foot range. The October 21 upslope catch shows why the relationship between contours can matter as much as any single depth. These results document where and how we fished on those dates; they do not establish a current bite at Cat Head or across Lake Marion.

NEXT STEP — November coverage will investigate a new location and compare its contours, bait, water conditions, sonar observations and actual fishing results against this October baseline. Public reports explain the general-area structure and reasoning; exact GPS positions and advanced tactics are available to Master Fisherman Patreon supporters.

DIVERSION CANAL FLOW ASSESSMENT — November 13, 2026 (11:48 a.m. EST)

STATUS: DIRECT CANAL FLOW NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. The Santee Cooper operator feed displays “Data last updated 11/13/2026”; its latest lake elevation observations are daily values for November 12, not instantaneous November 13 canal measurements. No direct, time-stamped Diversion Canal velocity, direction or discharge observation was verified. Independent USGS Marion Elloree (02169921) and Moultrie Pinopolis (02172000) gauge pages returned HTTP 403, preventing reconciliation of station datum and simultaneous observation times.

The differences are operator-data arithmetic, NOT independently verified comparable hydraulic head.

INTERPRETATION — CONDITIONAL ONLY: If Marion and Moultrie elevations are on the same datum and represent comparable observation times, the Marion-higher-than-Moultrie figures suggest a potential Marion-to-Moultrie hydraulic gradient. The modest nominal difference and its narrowing do not establish measured canal direction, current speed, or strength. Current canal flow remains NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED.

level_analysis: Daily lake-level readings above are published with USGS station timestamps. Review each gauge's vertical datum before comparing Lake Marion and Lake Moultrie. Water movement and reservoir operations require separate verification; elevation alone cannot establish canal discharge.
wind_analysis: The hourly wind forecast above provides broad guidance, but wind exposure varies by fetch, shoreline orientation, gusts and travel route. Check the selected forecast area, recheck conditions before launching, and do not treat a forecast as a measured on-water reading.
